title: The heart and blood
examples: What is the job of the heart?
How does blood travel around the body?
What is the difference between an artery and a vein?

explain.say: The heart has four chambers inside it. These chambers help pump blood around your body.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the human heart. Look at the right atrium, the right ventricle and the left atrium. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart to the body parts. They have thick, strong walls.
Veins carry deoxygenated blood back towards the heart. They have valves to stop backflow.
Capillaries are tiny vessels where oxygen moves from blood to cells. They are very narrow.
The double loop shows blood going to the lungs and then to the rest of the body. This is the full circuit.
When you exercise, your heart beats faster to pump more blood. This moves oxygen to your working muscles.

faq.a: The blood is red because it carries a substance called haemoglobin. Haemoglobin contains iron, which gives blood its colour.
asks: Where does the colour of blood come from?

faq.q: Does blood flow in one direction?
faq.a: Yes, the blood flow is carefully managed by the heart's valves. These valves open and close to ensure blood moves forward.
asks: How does the heart keep the blood moving?

faq.q: What is the difference between oxygenated and deoxygenated blood?
faq.a: Oxygenated blood has plenty of oxygen, usually leaving the lungs. Deoxygenated blood has less oxygen and more carbon dioxide.
asks: Which blood type goes to the lungs?
What is the job of oxygen in blood?

faq.q: Do all blood vessels carry blood?
faq.a: No, arteries carry blood away from the heart. Veins carry blood back to the heart. Capillaries connect them.
asks: What is the job of arteries versus veins?

faq.q: How does the double loop work?
faq.a: The first loop sends blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen. The second loop sends oxygenated blood to the body.
asks: What happens after blood leaves the heart?
Where does blood go after the lungs?

facts: The heart pumps blood through the circulatory system.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
Veins carry blood back to the heart.
Capillaries are the sites for gas exchange.

quiz.say: Blood leaves the heart through which vessels?
quiz.why: Arteries are defined as the vessels that carry blood away from the heart.

wrong.1: Veins carry blood back towards the heart, not away from it.
wrong.2: Capillaries are too small to be the main exit vessels from the heart.
wrong.3: Arterioles are smaller branches, but arteries are the main vessels leaving the heart.

quiz.say: Where does oxygen move from the blood?
quiz.why: Capillaries are the smallest vessels designed specifically for the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide.

wrong.0: Veins are mainly for returning waste blood to the heart.
wrong.1: The lungs are organs, not the specific vessel where the final exchange occurs.
wrong.3: Arteries carry oxygenated blood away, but the exchange happens in capillaries.

quiz.say: If the heart pumps blood to the lungs first, which vessels are involved in that path?
quiz.why: The pulmonary artery carries blood to the lungs, and the pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood back to the heart.

wrong.0: The return path from the lungs uses veins, not just arteries.
wrong.1: The path to the lungs must start with an artery carrying blood away.
wrong.3: The aorta goes to the body, and the vena cava comes from the body.
